subject: general
question:
PQRS is a cyclic quadrilateral in a circle with centre O. ∠PQR and ∠PSR are in the ratio

11 ∶ 7. If PQ = QR, then find. ∠OPQ
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Opposite angles in a cyclic quadrilateral sum to 180°. Let ∠PQR = 11x and ∠PSR = 7x.

11x + 7x = 180° ⇒ 18x = 180° ⇒ x = 10°. So, ∠PQR = 110° and ∠PSR = 70°.

In isosceles ΔPQR (PQ = QR): ∠QPR = (180° − 110°) ÷ 2 = 35°.

Central angle ∠POR = 2 × ∠PSR = 2 × 70° = 140°.

In isosceles ΔOPR (OP = OR): ∠OPR = (180° − 140°) ÷ 2 = 20°.

∠OPQ = ∠QPR + ∠OPR = 35° + 20° = 55°.

**∴ The correct answer is 55°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Cyclic quadrilateral** PQRS with center O. Ratio ∠PQR : ∠PSR = 11 : 7. Side **PQ = QR**.

**Formula Used:**

1. Sum of **opposite angles** of a cyclic quadrilateral is 180°.

2. Angle subtended by an arc at the center is **double** the angle subtended at the circumference.

3. In an **isosceles triangle**, angles opposite to equal sides are equal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1cae76ef0d456263dc1fe46e8e6d13d7cb310b6fe3b57cf8e42488323013f700.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ ∠PQR + ∠PSR = 180° (Opposite angles of cyclic quadrilateral)

⇒ 11k + 7k = 180° ⇒ 18k = 180° ⇒ k = 10°

⇒ ∠PQR = 110° and ∠PSR = 70°

⇒ In ΔPQR, PQ = QR ⇒ ∠QPR = ∠QRP

⇒ ∠QPR = (180° − 110°) ÷ 2 = 35°

⇒ ∠POR = 2 × ∠PSR = 2 × 70° = 140° (Angle at center property)

⇒ In ΔOPR, OP = OR (radii) ⇒ ∠OPR = ∠ORP

⇒ ∠OPR = (180° − 140°) ÷ 2 = 20°

⇒ Since ∠PQR > 90°, center O and vertex Q lie on opposite sides of chord PR.

⇒ ∠OPQ = ∠QPR + ∠OPR = 35° + 20° = 55°

**∴ The correct answer is 55°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cyclic Quadrilateral Theorems

The sum of opposite angles is 180°. The exterior angle is equal to the interior opposite angle.

Angle Subtended by a Chord

A chord subtends an angle at the center that is twice the angle it subtends at the major arc of the circumference.

Isosceles Property in Circles

Triangles formed by the center and any two points on the circumference (radii) are always isosceles.</p
